newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary helps flood-hit Polish, Czech children.
newsitem.headline: Hungary helps flood-hit Polish, Czech children.

text.p: Hungary is to provide a free summer camp for more than 1,000 children from the flood-stricken Czech Republic and Poland, officials of the Ministry for Industry, Trade and Tourism said on Tuesday.
"The idea to help the children came from our Prague and Warsaw representatives and the domestic response was very quick," ministry official Gyorgy Szekely told a news conference.
"Within a day of announcing our programme, 15 tourism companies offered their help."
Istvan Meggyes, general director of state-owned tourism promotion company Magyar Turizmus Rt, said Hungary will receive 680 children from Poland and 360 from the Czech Republic.
"Czech children, whose schools have been flooded, have asked for an opportunity to hold classes while here," Meggyes said. "They will have the necessary facilities".

Gyorgy Alexa, managing director of Hungarohostels Rt, which will provide accommodation for the Polish children in Bekes county, south-east Hungary, said several local organisations would also offer the children clothing or medical assistance.
"People in Bekes county still remember the floods that hit them in the seventies," Alexa said. "They want to help these children forget what they went through".
Hungary has provided 350 million forints ($1.8 million) worth of aid, mainly water pumps, blankets and clothing to the two countries, hit by the worst flooding this century.
